question: Refer to the exhibit. RTR_1 and RTR_2 exchange data-plane traffic directly, with N9K_1 through N9K_5 also participating in OSPF Area 0. An engineer must divert data-plane traffic between RTR_1 and RTR_2 to instead flow through N9K_4 and N9K_5, without forcing an OSPFv2 adjacency change. Which configuration, applied to the OSPF process 1 on N9K_2, accomplishes this goal?
context: Topology: RTR_1 and RTR_2 connect directly and also via N9K_1-N9K_5, all in OSPF Area 0.
imageNote: Diagram: Area 0 with RTR_2 - N9K_3 - (N9K_4, N9K_2, N9K_5) - N9K_1 - RTR_1, forming a diamond topology.
theory: The max-metric router-lsa command makes a router advertise all of its own router-LSA links, except stub links, with the maximum possible metric, so every other OSPF router in the area recalculates SPF and prefers alternate paths around that router for transit traffic — without the router dropping or resetting its OSPF adjacencies, so neighbors stay up and no re-negotiation occurs. This is the standard OSPF graceful-shutdown technique for draining transit traffic before maintenance, unlike changing administrative distance, filtering redistribution, or configuring a passive interface, none of which change how other routers calculate their best path through the topology. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 1 — OSPF Max-Metric Router-LSA)
